newsitem.title: UK: LME nickel touches 2-1/4 year low, copper weakens.
newsitem.headline: LME nickel touches 2-1/4 year low, copper weakens.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) nickel prices slumped to their lowest level since early October 1994 on Monday, weighed down by follow-through selling from last week, expectations of further stock rises and copper's weakness.
Copper stocks were also expected to rise again on Tuesday, helping to wipe $20 off the value of the red metal, which finished the afternoon kerb trading session at $2,130 a tonne.
Other base metals were quieter and narrowly mixed as the market wound down for the Christmas holiday.
The LME is closed on Tuesday afternoon, Wednesday and Thursday this week.
Nickel fell in fairly thin volumes, on what traders said was general long liquidation.
"One particular player was lending the spreads as well as selling three months, and it looked like a bit of long liquidation," said one trader.
Nickel bottomed at $6,500, down $130 from Friday's afternoon kerb before recovering slightly to end the day at $6,515.
Demand from the stainless steel industry, which consumes two thirds of the world's nickel, has been weak for several months, and LME stocks are rising towards the psychological 50,000-tonne level.
Traders said support from the market should emerge on any further tests of $6,500, but a break below it could prompt a fresh wave of selling towards $6,330.
Copper fell in light volumes, with stocks expected to show an increase on Tuesday.

Spreads also narrowed, with cash easing to a $90 premium over three months by the midsession break before firming to $100 by the afternoon close. This was still below Friday's closing level of around $107 backwardation.
Aluminium was sluggish, slipping into the minus column by the close to end $1.50 weaker at $1,550.
Lead lost $7 to $707 while zinc edged higher to $1,066 from $1,065.50 on Friday.
Tin also made modest gains, ending the afternoon up $20 at $5,790. Alloy was last quoted at $1,390/400, unchanged from Friday.
